They reported that 95.2% of mothers in the intervention-access study continued to access services through the final follow-up, compared with 33.7% in an earlier referral model where mothers had been asked to visit a mental-health facility.

The finding suggests that where care is offered can matter.

For mothers who already visit health facilities for their babies' immunisations and other services, bringing appropriate mental-health support into those settings may reduce some of the barriers associated with referral to a separate specialist facility.

---

WHAT NEEDS TO CHANGE?

Postpartum depression cannot be addressed simply by telling mothers to “be strong.”

Families need better awareness of the signs.

Healthcare workers need to recognise women who may be struggling.

Mental-health support needs to become easier to access, particularly through services mothers already use.

And mothers need to know that asking for help does not make them bad mothers.

WHO guidance supports integrating maternal mental-health care into general healthcare, including maternal and child-health services, while Nigerian research suggests that culturally appropriate and community-based approaches may help improve access.

The challenge is therefore not only treating women once they become severely unwell.

It is recognising the problem earlier, reducing stigma and making appropriate support easier to reach.

---

SHE DOES NOT HAVE TO SUFFER IN SILENCE

For a woman struggling with postpartum depression, recovery may begin with something that sounds simple but can be difficult to find:

Someone who listens.

That person could be a partner, family member, community health worker, doctor or mental-health professional.

What matters is that her distress is taken seriously.

The research from Nigeria offers reasons for hope. The 2025 Jos trial found that a culturally adapted psychological intervention was acceptable to participating mothers and showed preliminary evidence of reducing depression and anxiety, while earlier Nigerian research demonstrated that bringing intervention services into primary healthcare settings could improve access.

But research also shows why the conversation cannot stop at treatment.

Stigma, family decision-making, social expectations and access to services can all shape whether a woman receives care in the first place.

The birth of a baby is often described as one of life's happiest moments.

But for some mothers, it can also mark the beginning of a difficult and lonely period that other people cannot see

Postpartum depression does not make a woman a bad mother.

Sometimes, she is simply a mother who needs someone to notice that she is struggling — and help her find her way back.

title: 5 Skills Every Young Nigerian Can Learn With Just a Phone
excerpt: "No laptop? You can still learn useful digital skills, build experience, and start working toward an income."
content:
Everyone keeps saying, “Learn a skill.”

Sounds easy until you realise you don’t have a laptop. Maybe you’re still in school. Maybe money is tight. Maybe your phone is the only device you have right now.

That doesn’t mean you have to wait.

There are several skills you can learn with just your phone, especially if you’re willing to practise consistently. You may not become an expert overnight, but you can start building a skill that could eventually turn into paid work.

Here are five digital skills worth learning in Nigeria right now.

1. Copywriting

If you can write a caption that makes someone stop scrolling, you already have a starting point.

Copywriting is the art of using words to persuade people to take action whether that means buying a product, clicking a link, signing up for something, or simply paying attention.

And yes, you can learn copywriting with your phone.

Try this: find a boring product description online and rewrite it. Make it clearer, more interesting, and more persuasive. Do this regularly and compare your old writing with your newer attempts.

Over time, you'll start understanding what makes people pay attention.

2. Graphic Design

You don't need Photoshop or an expensive computer to start learning graphic design.

Apps such as Canva allow beginners to create flyers, social media graphics, posters and simple brand designs directly from a phone.

But don't confuse using Canva with being a designer. The app gives you the tools; you still need to learn things like layout, spacing, typography and visual hierarchy.

Start by recreating designs you see online. Then create your own versions. The goal isn't to make something complicated. It's to learn what makes a design look clean and professional.

3. Social Media Management

Businesses need people who understand how to manage their social media pages.

That involves much more than posting pictures.

A social media manager may create content, schedule posts, respond to comments and messages, study audience behaviour, and help a brand increase its reach and engagement.

If you're already comfortable using Instagram, Facebook, TikTok or other platforms, you have a useful starting point.

The difference is learning to use social media strategically, rather than just scrolling through it.

You can practise by choosing a small business and creating a sample one-week content plan for them.

4. Virtual Assistance

Virtual assistance is another skill you can begin learning without a laptop.

Small businesses and entrepreneurs often need help with tasks such as replying to messages, managing emails, organising information, scheduling appointments and handling customer enquiries.

A smartphone, internet connection and good communication skills can be enough for some beginner-level tasks.

Start by learning how to organise information properly, write professional messages and manage basic tasks using tools available on your phone.

Being reliable matters just as much as being technically skilled.

5. Voiceover and Content Narration

If you have a clear voice and somewhere reasonably quiet to record, voiceover work is another option to explore.

Businesses and content creators use voiceovers for advertisements, explainer videos, social media content and other digital projects.

You don't need expensive recording equipment to begin practising. Your phone's voice recorder can be enough for your first attempts.

Record yourself reading different types of scripts. Listen back and work on your pronunciation, pacing, clarity and tone.

Eventually, you can put your best samples together into a simple demo reel.

You Don't Need a Laptop to Start Learning

A laptop can certainly make some things easier. But waiting until you can afford one before learning anything is a mistake.

Your phone can be a learning tool, practice tool and communication tool.

The harder part isn't finding a skill to learn. It's choosing one, practising consistently and getting good enough to offer it to someone else.

Don't try to learn all five at once.

Pick one skill, spend the next few weeks practising it, create a few samples of your work, and start looking for opportunities to use it.

Your first attempt will probably be bad.

That's normal.

The important thing is that you make the first attempt.

Which skill would you start with if your phone was the only tool you had? Tell us in the comments.

title: Building a Real-Time Collaborative Notification Engine with WebSockets and Node.js
excerpt: Step-by-step tutorial on architecting a scalable real-time notification engine with Node.js, Redis Pub/Sub, and WebSocket connections.
content:
Building a Real-Time Collaborative Notification Engine with WebSockets and Node.js

Modern interactive applications require immediate real-time updates for notifications, live comments, and collaborative editing. In this comprehensive tutorial, we will build a scalable real-time notification hub utilizing WebSockets and Redis Pub/Sub.

Why Redis Pub/Sub for WebSockets?

A single WebSocket server works fine on a single machine, but when your application scales horizontally across multiple serverless containers or instances, user A connected to Server 1 cannot receive events emitted from Server 2. Redis Pub/Sub acts as the universal event message bus connecting all server instances.

Step 1: Setting Up the WebSocket Gateway

import { WebSocketServer, WebSocket } from 'ws';
import Redis from 'ioredis';

const wss = new WebSocketServer({ port: 8080 });
const redisSub = new Redis(process.env.REDIS_URL);
const clients = new Map<string, WebSocket>();

wss.on('connection', (ws, req) => {
  const userId = extractUserIdFromCookie(req);
  if (userId) {
    clients.set(userId, ws);
  }

  ws.on('close', () => {
    if (userId) clients.delete(userId);
  });
});

// Subscribe to Redis Notification Channel
redisSub.subscribe('user-notifications', (err) => {
  if (err) console.error('Failed to subscribe:', err);
});

redisSub.on('message', (channel, message) => {
  if (channel === 'user-notifications') {
    const payload = JSON.parse(message);
    const targetSocket = clients.get(payload.targetUserId);
    if (targetSocket && targetSocket.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) {
      targetSocket.send(JSON.stringify(payload.notification));
    }
  }
});

Step 2: Emitting Events from API Route Handlers

import Redis from 'ioredis';
const redisPub = new Redis(process.env.REDIS_URL);

export async function sendNotification(targetUserId: string, message: string) {
  const payload = {
    targetUserId,
    notification: {
      id: crypto.randomUUID(),
      message,
      timestamp: new Date().toISOString()
    }
  };
  await redisPub.publish('user-notifications', JSON.stringify(payload));
}

Step 3: Resilient Client-Side Connection Management

On the browser client, always implement exponential backoff reconnection strategies with heartbeat ping/pong signals to recover automatically from transient network interruptions.

title: It Was Never Just About Yam
excerpt: The ancient meaning behind the Igbo New Yam Festival
content:
The first yam came out of the earth just before sunrise.

Obinna knew because his father had told him not to touch it.

For weeks, he had watched the leaves of the yam vines spread across their farmland, green and stubborn against the reddish soil. Every morning, he followed his father to the farm, hoping that today would be the day they finally dug one up.

But his father always shook his head. “Not yet.”

So when the day finally came, Obinna was almost disappointed.

His father crouched beside the mound, pushed his fingers into the loose earth and carefully uncovered the yam. He brushed away the soil slowly.

There it was, large, smooth and fresh from the earth.

Obinna's eyes widened. “Papa, can we cook it?”

His father laughed. “Cook it?”

“Yes.”

His father shook his head. “Not until the elders say so.”

Obinna frowned. “But it is our yam.”

“It is,” his father said. “But the first yam does not belong only to us.”

Later that morning, the news travelled through the village.

The yam had come and suddenly, everything changed.

Women began preparing food. Men returned from their farms earlier than usual. Children ran through the compounds carrying messages. The sound of drums drifted through the village.

People who had travelled away began coming home.

Fine clothes were brought out. Compounds were swept. Food was prepared in quantities large enough to feed far more people than lived in the household and somewhere in the middle of all the noise, Obinna finally understood why his father had refused to cook that yam.

It wasn't simply food.

It was a beginning of a new harvest, a reason to gather and give thanks to Chukwu Okike and for the people whose lives had long been deeply connected to the land, that was no small thing.

It was never just about yam.

The Igbo New Yam Festival, known by different names in different communities, including Iri Ji and Iwa Ji, traditionally marks the arrival of the new yam harvest but why was one crop important enough to have an entire festival dedicated to it?

Because yam was far more than something to put in a pot.

For many traditional Igbo communities, a successful yam harvest meant food, survival and prosperity. Growing it required considerable labour, patience and skill. A good harvest could also bring social recognition and the ability to provide for others.

So the arrival of the new harvest was a moment worth marking.

The old season was ending and a new one was beginning.

Before the new yam was eaten, ceremonies could be performed to give thanks and formally welcome the harvest. The exact practices differed between communities, because Igboland was never one single society with identical customs.

There will be celebration, drums, dancing, feasting, family and of course, yam. Lots of tubers.

But perhaps one of the most beautiful parts of the tradition is the way it brings people home.

Even today, people who live far from their ancestral communities may travel back for New Yam celebrations. The festival has changed with time, but that connection to home remains because beneath the food and festivities is a simple message:

We survived another season.

The earth provided.

The farmers worked.

The community gathered and there is another season ahead.

That is why the New Yam Festival isn't merely a celebration of a crop.

It is a celebration of life, labour, gratitude and belonging.

So the next time you see an Igbo New Yam celebration, look beyond the dancing and the plates of pounded yam.

There is a history sitting on that plate.

A history of people whose relationship with the land was woven into their food, their traditions and their sense of community.

Obinna's father was right.

The first yam never belonged only to them.

It belonged to the story of everyone who had waited for it.

title: "Big bum bum doesn't matter.”
excerpt: Ahhh! It does oo. 😂
content:
Before you start dragging me, hear me out.

In Nigeria right now, especially in the entertainment and social media space, people can attribute a surprising amount of value to a woman's body shape. Sometimes, it feels like having a big backside has become part of the unofficial requirements for being considered attractive, successful, or even worthy of attention and honestly, some ladies have started believing it too.

You hear things like, “I need to add weight,” “I need to get my body done,” or “Nobody will notice me with this kind of body.”

But what about the women with small bum bum?

Are they supposed to believe they cannot achieve anything because their backside isn't doing enough?

Even some men have made it a major factor in deciding whether they will approach a woman or not. If the bum bum is small, apparently the application has been rejected before the interview and this is where it gets interesting because while we're laughing about it, there is a real pressure behind all of this.

Social media has made certain body types look like the standard. We constantly see women with tiny waists, big hips and very noticeable backsides, and after seeing that image repeatedly, some people begin to feel like their natural bodies are somehow inadequate.

For some women, it doesn't stop at wishing they looked different. They actually go as far as undergoing cosmetic procedures, including Brazilian Butt Lifts (BBLs), to achieve the body they believe will finally make them feel beautiful, desirable or accepted and let's be clear: wanting cosmetic surgery is a personal decision. Nobody should be shamed for making a choice about their own body but we also shouldn't pretend that these procedures are completely harmless.

BBL is a major surgical procedure and, like other surgeries, it comes with risks. Complications can include infection, bleeding, reactions to anaesthesia and, in severe cases, fat embolism, which can be life-threatening.

So before we turn a particular body shape into the price of admission for beauty, maybe we should ask ourselves: Who decided this was the standard in the first place?

Having a big bum bum may get you more attention in certain spaces. It may influence how some people perceive you. It may even open certain doors in industries where appearance is heavily emphasized.

So if I hear someone say, “Big bum bum doesn't matter,” I might actually break their head.

Because ahhh...

It does oo.

But your bum bum should never be the reason you believe you have value.

Small bum bum oo, big bum bum, the somewhere-in-between own oo 😭, we are all still going to pay our bills and mind our business.

Share and Like 😘

title:
The AI Advantage: Why Your Expertise Still Matters
‎
excerpt: ‎There is a great shift happening in workplaces all over the world. ‎This is not just about AI being capable of carrying out more tasks. It is that knowing how …
content:
‎There is a great shift happening in workplaces all over the world.

‎This is not just about AI being capable of carrying out more tasks. It is that knowing how to work with AI is becoming part of how we work.

‎‎For a very long time, professional growth has been restricted to a single path: get a degree, develop skills, gain experience and become good at what you do.

‎‎Of course, those things still matter.

‎‎But how we apply that knowledge and the tools we use to apply that knowledge are rapidly changing.

‎‎Today, A scientist can use AI to analyse datasets, explore biological sequences and accelerate research.

‎‎A data analyst can use it to identify repeated patterns in strings of data and automate reports and insights.

‎‎A programmer can use it to understand unfamiliar code, debug code errors and design prototype solutions.

‎‎A writer can use it to expand research, brainstorm and refine novel ideas. The applications of AI are limitless today.

‎‎So perhaps the more important question is no longer:

‎‎“Will AI take over human jobs?”

‎‎Rather, the appropriate question should be:

‎‎“What can I accomplish when I know how to work with AI efficiently?”

‎‎But there is a huge difference between using AI and understanding AI.

‎‎You can ask AI to analyse data sets but  can you recognize when the analysis is wrong?

‎‎You can prompt AI to summarize a scientific paper but can you detect a fabricated reference?

‎‎You can ask it to write code but can you understand the code and test it to see what it produces?

‎‎One thing with AI is that it can generate rapid outputs but human expertise is still needed to question, verify and apply those outputs/results appropriately.

‎‎We now have emerging fields of scientific research combining AI with laboratory expertise.

‎‎Examples include:

  • ‎‎Genomics + Machine Learning (ML)

  • ‎Drug discovery + computational modeling

  • ‎Microbiology + Artificial intelligence (AI)

  • ‎Environmental science + predictive analytics

  • ‎Public health + data science

  • ‎Synthetic biology + computational tools

‎And many others.

‎‎These are no longer isolated words rather they are fields where latest technology and science intersect.

‎‎This presents an opportunity for students and professionals which does not necessarily require them to abandon your existing field to become AI-ready.

‎‎But to explore tools to extend basic expertise with technology.

‎‎The goal isn't to learn every AI tool that appears.

‎‎It is to have a great understanding of your field deeply,

‎‎To be able to identify where technology can improve your work,

‎‎To be ready to learn how to use AI effectively,

‎‎And to develop the critical thinking needed to verify its results.

‎‎The only constant thing is change and die to that, the future of work will continue to evolve.

‎‎Some tasks will be fully automated with AI agents, others redesigned, and new opportunities will emerge.

‎‎Our advantage then will not come from competing with AI at everything it can do.

‎‎It will definitely come from learning how to combine human expertise, critical thinking, creativity and AI.

‎‎The future is not necessarily humans versus AI.

‎‎It could be:

‎‎Humans + AI = Skyrocketing productivity.

‎‎And the time to start building that combination is NOW!!!.

‎

title: Nobody Warned Us About How Lonely Adulthood Would Feel.
excerpt: Growing up was supposed to mean freedom. Nobody told us it could also mean losing friends, carrying silent struggles, and sometimes feeling alone even when you're surrounded by people.
content:
When we were children, adulthood looked beautiful.

We couldn't wait to grow up.

We imagined having our own money, making our own decisions, going wherever we wanted, and finally being free from adults telling us what to do.

Nobody showed us the part where friendships become harder to maintain.

Nobody explained that the people you once spoke to every day could slowly become strangers.

Nobody warned us that you could have hundreds of contacts in your phone and still stare at your screen, wondering who you could call when life becomes too heavy.

And perhaps the strangest part is that nobody necessarily did anything wrong.

Sometimes, people simply grew up.

Life became busy.

Responsibilities arrived.

And somewhere between work, money, family, relationships, and trying to build a future, we started losing the effortless friendships we once took for granted.

That's the loneliness nobody prepared us for.

title: 3 AI Prompts Every Executive Should Use Before 9 AM
excerpt: Your morning routine can determine how much control you have over the rest of your day.For executives, founders, and business leaders, mornings often begin with…
content:
Your morning routine can determine how much control you have over the rest of your day.

For executives, founders, and business leaders, mornings often begin with a crowded calendar, unread emails, messages, deadlines, and meetings.

The problem isn't always a lack of time. It is often a lack of clarity.

Before 9 AM, you should know what needs your attention, which meetings matter most, and which tasks can wait or be delegated.

This is where AI prompts for executives can be useful.

Instead of spending the first hour of your day sorting through information manually, you can use AI to organize your tasks, prepare for meetings, and manage your inbox.

Here are three simple AI productivity prompts to try before 9 AM.

1. Use AI to Identify Your Top 3 Priorities

Prompt:

“Review my calendar and task list for today. Identify my top 3 priorities, explain why they matter, and suggest what I should focus on first.”

A long task list doesn't tell you what deserves your attention first.

You may have a presentation to prepare, a client waiting for a response, several meetings, administrative work, and dozens of emails.

Treating everything as equally important can leave you busy without making meaningful progress.

This prompt helps you narrow your day down to three priorities.

For example, AI might help you identify:

  • Reviewing a proposal that needs approval today

  • Preparing for an important client meeting

  • Approving a project budget before the deadline

The rest of your tasks may still matter, but these three have a stronger reason to come first.

You can make the prompt even more specific:

“Rank today's tasks by urgency, business impact, and deadline. Give me only the top 3 priorities and explain your ranking.”

This is particularly useful for executive productivity because it gives you a starting point before other people's requests begin taking over your schedule.

Why it works

Executives make dozens of decisions every day. Knowing what deserves attention first makes it easier to protect time for high-value work.

The goal isn't to complete every task immediately.

The goal is to make sure your most important work doesn't get pushed aside by less important tasks.

2. Use AI to Prepare for Your First Important Meeting

Prompt:

“Review the information I have about my 9 AM meeting and create a brief with the meeting objective, key discussion points, decisions required, questions I should ask, and expected next steps.”

Meetings are a major part of an executive's schedule.

But attending a meeting and being prepared for it are two different things.

A five-minute briefing before an important meeting can help you understand what needs to happen before the conversation even starts.

For example, if you're meeting with a client about a project, your AI-generated briefing could include:

Meeting objective:
Agree on the next phase of the project.

Key discussion points:
Project progress, outstanding issues, timeline, and budget.

Decisions required:
Approve the revised timeline and project scope.

Questions to ask:
Have the client's priorities changed?

Next steps:
Confirm responsibilities and deadlines.

Instead of searching through old emails, documents, and meeting notes minutes before the call, you have the key information in one place.

This AI meeting preparation workflow can be useful for:

  • Client meetings

  • Team meetings

  • Project reviews

  • Sales calls

  • Interviews

  • Strategy sessions

  • Partnership discussions

The quality of the result depends on the information you provide. If you have previous meeting notes, project documents, an agenda, or relevant emails, include them in your AI workflow.

AI can organize the information, but you remain responsible for the decisions and direction of the meeting.

3. Use AI to Triage Your Inbox

Prompt:

“Review my unread emails and categorize them into urgent, important, delegate, and informational. For urgent and important emails, summarize what is needed and recommend the next action.”

Your inbox can quickly become one of the biggest distractions in your morning.

An email arrives, you respond. Another arrives, you open it. Then you discover an older message that needs attention.

Before you realize it, you've spent an hour answering emails instead of working on your priorities.

This is where AI for email management can help.

Instead of immediately responding to every message, start by sorting your inbox into four categories:

Urgent

Requires your attention as soon as possible.

Important

Needs your response but doesn't require immediate action.

Delegate

Can be handled by an assistant, team member, or another person.

Informational

Useful information that doesn't require a response.

For example, a client requesting an approval before the end of the day may be urgent.

A team member requesting feedback for next week's presentation may be important.

A routine scheduling request could be delegated.

A newsletter may simply be informational.

This simple system can help you spend less time deciding what every email means and more time acting on the messages that actually matter.

You can also ask AI to draft responses to selected emails.

However, always review AI-generated responses before sending them, particularly when the message involves clients, employees, finances, confidential information, or important business decisions.


A Simple 15-Minute AI Morning Routine

You don't need a complicated productivity system.

Try turning these three prompts into a 15-minute morning routine.

Minutes 1–5: Review your priorities

Look at your calendar and task list.

Identify the three tasks or outcomes that matter most.

Minutes 5–10: Prepare for your key meeting

Create a short meeting briefing.

Know the objective, important discussion points, decisions required, and next steps.

Minutes 10–15: Triage your inbox

Sort unread emails into urgent, important, delegate, and informational.

Respond only to the messages that require your attention now.

Then move on.

How Executives Can Use AI Without Losing Control

AI can help with many parts of an executive's workflow, but it shouldn't become another source of noise.

The most useful approach is to give AI a specific job.

Instead of asking:

“How can AI make my day more productive?”

Give it a clear task:

“Identify my top three priorities.”

“Prepare me for this meeting.”

“Sort these emails by urgency.”

Specific prompts usually produce more useful results because the task and expected outcome are clear.

This is also why AI prompts for business leaders should be connected to real work.

Use your calendar, task list, meeting notes, project information, and relevant emails as context where appropriate.

The better the context, the more useful the output is likely to be.

The Real Benefit of an AI Morning Routine

The value of these prompts isn't simply saving a few minutes.

It's starting your day with a clear understanding of where your attention should go.

Instead of opening your inbox and allowing incoming messages to determine your priorities, you begin with a plan.

Instead of entering a meeting wondering what needs to be discussed, you have a briefing.

Instead of looking at a long task list, you have three priorities.

That can make your morning more intentional and reduce the amount of time spent on low-value administrative work.

Final Thought

You don't need dozens of AI tools to improve your productivity.

Start with three useful prompts:

What are my top three priorities today?

What do I need to accomplish in my most important meeting?

Which emails actually need my attention?

Spend 15 minutes answering those questions before 9 AM.

Then use the rest of your morning to execute.

AI shouldn't replace your judgment. It should help you spend more time using it.

What AI prompts do you use to organize your workday?

Share it in the comments.

Follow Echo Gist for more practical insights on AI, productivity, digital tools, career growth, and the future of work.

title: What Is the Purpose of Life? Why You Feel Lost, Stuck, and Unsure About Your Future
excerpt:
Questioning the purpose of life, feeling stuck, or wondering whether you are falling behind does not necessarily mean something is wrong with you. Sometimes, it simply means you are growing, changing, and beginning to recognize that the life you once wanted may no longer be the life you need.

The biggest takeaway is this: you can be grateful for your life and still want more from it. You do not have to have your entire future figured out, meet society’s timeline, or discover one perfect purpose overnight. Life is a process of becoming, and meaning can be found in the people we love, the work we do, the lives we touch, the lessons we learn, and the person we gradually become.

You may not be behind. You may simply be living a life in progress.
content:
Have you ever looked at your life and quietly wondered, “What am I actually doing with my life?” You are not the only one.

Most days, life is beautiful.

You wake up and realize you still have reasons to be grateful. You thank God. You look at how far you have come and think, “Wow. I really made it through that.”

You remember the things you once prayed for.

The things you once cried about.

The things you thought you would never survive.

And somehow, you are here.

Still standing.

Still breathing.

Still becoming.

A life in progress.

But then there are other days.

The trembling days.

The days when gratitude and confusion somehow sit at the same table.

You are grateful for how far you have come, but somewhere inside you, another question quietly appears:

“Is this all there is?”

And immediately, you feel guilty for asking.

Because how can you say you want more when you have already received so much?

How can you complain when someone else is praying for the exact life you currently have?

So you silence yourself.

You tell yourself to be grateful.

And you are.

You really are.

But gratitude does not always mean you have stopped wanting more.

Sometimes, it simply means you appreciate where you are while recognizing that you may have outgrown where you are.

Why Do I Feel Lost in Life Even When Everything Looks Fine?

There was a time when this stage of your life was everything you wanted.

The job.

The relationship.

The apartment.

The salary.

The independence.

The little achievements nobody else understood.

You were so excited to get here.

And then, somehow, you arrived.

But it doesn't feel the way you imagined it would.

Nothing is necessarily wrong.

Yet something feels different.

You have changed.

Your dreams have changed.

Your priorities have changed.

Your definition of success has changed.

The things that once excited you don't excite you in the same way anymore.

And now you are standing inside a life you once prayed for, wondering why your heart is asking for something else.

Maybe that is one of the strangest parts of growing up.

Sometimes you outgrow things you once begged God for.

And that does not automatically make you ungrateful.

It makes you human.

Growing is not always about getting more.

Sometimes, it is about realizing that what you once wanted no longer fits the person you are becoming.

What to Do When You Feel Stuck in Life

Then come the days when nothing seems to work.

You tried.

You really did.

You made the plans.

You worked hard.

You showed up.

You prayed.

You sacrificed.

You tried to do things the right way — or at least what you believed was the right way.

And somehow, everything still became slow.

The application went unanswered.

The business refused to grow.

The opportunity passed.

The relationship ended.

The money disappeared almost as quickly as it came.

You watched people you started with move ahead.

Someone bought a house.

Someone got married.

Someone moved abroad.

Someone had a baby.

Someone got the promotion.

Someone became successful at twenty-six.

And you?

You are still trying to figure out what you are doing.

You smile when people ask:

“How far?”

But sometimes the honest answer is:

“I don't even know.”

Maybe you feel stuck because you expected your life to move according to a particular timeline.

School by this age.

Career by that age.

Marriage by another age.

Children.

House.

Money.

Success.

And when reality refuses to follow the timeline, you begin wondering whether something is wrong with you.

But being stuck is not always the same as being behind.

Sometimes it is simply a season where you are being forced to reconsider where you are going.

Am I Behind in Life?

This is where comparison becomes dangerous.

Because you are looking at somebody else's chapter while reading your own unfinished sentence.

You see their announcement.

You don't see their anxiety.

You see the new job.

You don't see the years of rejection.

You see the wedding pictures.

You don't see the private battles.

You see the achievement.

You don't see the road that led there.

Social media makes this even harder.

Every time you open your phone, someone seems to be moving forward.

New job.

New car.

New house.

Engagement.

Wedding.

Baby.

Business launch.

International trip.

Promotion.

Another person announcing another achievement.

Meanwhile, you are sitting in your room wondering why your own life feels like it has paused.

But perhaps your life isn't late.

Perhaps it is simply unfolding differently.

Your timeline is not a universal deadline.

Someone else's progress does not erase yours.

And becoming often takes much longer than we were told it would.

The Questions About Life We Don't Say Out Loud

Sometimes, when everything becomes quiet, the questions become loud.

Did I make the right decision?

Should I have taken that opportunity?

Should I have stayed?

Should I have left?

What exactly am I doing with my life?

Why am I here?

What is the purpose of my life?

These questions can feel frightening because they don't always have immediate answers.

We wake up.

We work.

We try to make money.

We pay bills.

We struggle.

We rest.

We wake up again.

We try again.

Some people fall in love.

Some become parents.

Some don't.

Some become wealthy.

Some spend their entire lives trying to survive.

Some achieve everything they dreamed about.

Others never even get the opportunity to begin.

And eventually, every human life comes to an end.

So sometimes you sit quietly and wonder:

Is this really what life is?

Work.

Survive.

Earn.

Spend.

Repeat.

And then one day, disappear.

Do we live only to die?

Or are we supposed to actually live somewhere between the beginning and the end?

These questions may not mean you have lost your way.

Sometimes, they mean you have started paying attention.

What Is the Purpose of Life?

Perhaps we are asking the wrong question.

Maybe the purpose of life is not something that suddenly arrives one morning with a notification saying:

“Congratulations. You have discovered your purpose.”

Maybe purpose is something we build.

In the people we love.

In the lives we touch.

In the work we do.

In the things we create.

In the kindness we give.

In the lessons we learn.

In the person we become.

For some people, purpose is deeply connected to faith and serving God.

For others, it may be found through family, creativity, career, service, relationships, learning or helping other people.

And for many of us, it may change throughout different seasons of life.

Maybe your life doesn't have to look extraordinary every day to be meaningful.

Maybe that ordinary Tuesday you spent laughing with someone you love mattered.

Maybe helping someone mattered.

Maybe surviving that difficult season mattered.

Maybe getting out of bed when you didn't feel like trying anymore mattered.

Maybe becoming a softer, wiser and stronger version of yourself matters.

We spend so much time looking for one huge reason to exist that we sometimes overlook the small reasons that keep us going.

How to Find Your Purpose in Life When You Feel Lost

You may not discover your purpose by sitting around waiting for a perfect answer.

Sometimes, you find direction by paying attention.

Ask yourself:

What do I care about deeply?

What kind of problems do I want to solve?

What makes me feel alive?

What experiences have shaped me?

What am I naturally drawn toward?

Who do I want to become?

What kind of impact do I want my life to have?

You don't need to answer all of these questions today.

You may not even have the answers yet.

And that is okay.

Sometimes purpose becomes clearer while you are moving, not while you are waiting.

You Are Allowed to Want More

You can be grateful and still want more.

You can love your life and still desire change.

You can appreciate your journey and still admit that you are tired.

You can thank God for what you have while praying for what you don't.

You can be proud of yourself and still know there is more inside you.

Those things can exist together.

Wanting more does not automatically mean you don't appreciate what you already have.

Sometimes, wanting more is simply recognizing that you are still growing.

Life isn't always a straight line.

Sometimes it is a circle.

Sometimes it feels like a dead end.

Sometimes you take three steps forward and somehow find yourself standing in the same place again.

But perhaps progress isn't always about moving faster.

Sometimes progress is simply becoming someone who can handle the next version of your life.

If You Feel Lost, Remember This

If you are currently questioning your choices...

If you feel stuck...

If you feel like everyone is moving while you are standing still...

If you are grateful but still hungry for more...

If you don't know what the next chapter looks like...

Take a breath.

You don't have to have everything figured out today.

You don't have to know exactly where your career is going.

You don't have to have the perfect relationship.

You don't have to meet every milestone at the age society expects.

You don't have to understand your entire life before you are allowed to live it.

You are still becoming.

And perhaps that is the most honest thing any of us can say about life.

A life in progress.

Hey.

It's you.

Still learning.

Still healing.

Still hoping.

Still trying.

Still becoming.

A living life in progress.

Maybe you don't need to know exactly where the story ends.

Maybe, for now, you just need to keep living the next page.

title: You Are Not Behind — You Are Building
excerpt: There is a quiet pressure that comes with growing older.You open social media and see someone getting a new job.Someone is launching a business.Someone is trave…
content:
There is a quiet pressure that comes with growing older.

You open social media and see someone getting a new job.

Someone is launching a business.

Someone is travelling.

Someone is getting married.

Someone is buying a car.

Someone seems to have everything figured out.

And then you look at your own life and wonder:

“Am I behind?”

Maybe you are.

Or maybe you are simply looking at someone else's chapter while judging yourself by their highlight.

The truth is, life does not come with one timetable.

Some people find their direction at 20. Others find it at 30. Some people get their first major opportunity early. Others spend years learning, failing, starting again, and trying different things before something finally works.

That doesn't mean they failed.

It means their journey looks different.

Stop Measuring Your Life Against Someone Else's Timeline

Comparison can make you forget how far you've come.

Maybe you don't have the job you want yet, but you've developed a skill.

Maybe your business isn't where you want it to be, but you finally started.

Maybe you haven't achieved your biggest goal, but you're no longer the person you were two years ago.

Those things matter.

Progress isn't always loud.

Sometimes progress looks like waking up and trying again.

Sometimes it looks like studying when you're tired.

Sometimes it looks like applying for another opportunity after being rejected.

Sometimes it looks like learning a skill nobody around you understands yet.

And sometimes, progress simply means refusing to give up.

Your Small Steps Are Still Taking You Somewhere

We often expect progress to look dramatic.

But most meaningful growth happens quietly.

One page becomes a finished course.

One skill becomes a portfolio.

One connection becomes an opportunity.

One small idea becomes a business.

One decision to keep going becomes the beginning of a completely different life.

Don't underestimate small beginnings.

You don't need to have everything figured out before you start building.

Give Yourself Permission to Grow Slowly

You are allowed to learn.

You are allowed to change your mind.

You are allowed to start again.

You are allowed to be a beginner.

You are allowed to take longer than someone else.

What matters is that you keep moving.

Your journey doesn't become less valuable because someone else's journey appears faster.

You are not behind.

You are learning.

You are growing.

You are building.

And one day, you may look back and realize that the season you thought was taking you nowhere was actually preparing you for where you were going.

So breathe.

Keep learning.

Keep trying.

Keep building.

Your timeline is still your timeline.

A Question for You

What is one thing you're currently working on that nobody may notice yet—but you believe will make a difference in your future?

Share it in the comments. Someone else might be on the same journey.

title: 5 Relationship Red Flags That Look Like Love at First
excerpt: Some things feel like love in the beginning. Pay attention to what they become.
content:
Not every relationship red flag arrives looking like a red flag.

Sometimes, it looks like someone who wants to know where you are because they “care.”

Sometimes, it looks like jealousy because “they don't want to lose you.”

Sometimes, it even looks like someone being extremely involved in every part of your life.

At first, it can feel flattering.

Then, little by little, you realise it isn't affection anymore. It's control.

Here are five relationship red flags that are easy to mistake for love.

1. They Want to Know Everything About You

At first, constant calls and messages can feel sweet.

They want to know where you are, who you're with and what you're doing.

But there's a difference between genuine interest and monitoring.

If they expect your location at all times, demand access to your phone, question every person you speak to or get angry whenever you don't respond immediately, that's not automatically love.

Attention becomes control when you are no longer free to say no.

2. Their Jealousy Is Presented as Proof of Love

“You're lucky I love you this much.”

“I just don't like other people getting too close to you.”

“I get jealous because I care.”

We've heard versions of these statements before.

A little jealousy may happen in relationships. The problem is when jealousy becomes an excuse for controlling what you wear, who you talk to, where you go or who you are allowed to be friends with.

Someone can love you and still respect your freedom.

If their version of love requires you to constantly prove that you're loyal, pay attention.

3. They Make You Feel Guilty for Having Boundaries

You say you don't like something.

Instead of respecting it, they make you feel guilty for saying no.

You need some time alone?

“You're becoming distant.”

You don't want to share your password?

“So you must be hiding something.”

You don't want to do something you're uncomfortable with?

“If you really loved me, you would.”

That last sentence is especially dangerous.

Love should not be used as a bargaining chip to make you ignore your own boundaries.

4. They Make You Question Your Own Memory

You bring up something that happened.

They deny it.

You explain how their words affected you.

Suddenly, you're “too sensitive.”

You remember the conversation clearly, but somehow you end up apologising for bringing it up.

This can become a pattern of emotional manipulation.

Not every disagreement means someone is gaslighting you. People genuinely remember situations differently sometimes.

But if someone repeatedly twists conversations, denies obvious behaviour and makes you constantly doubt your own perception, don't ignore the pattern.

5. You Are Always Walking on Eggshells

This one is easy to overlook because nothing dramatic may be happening.

You're simply always careful.

You think about how to phrase every message.

You avoid certain topics because you know they'll become angry.

You apologise even when you don't believe you did anything wrong.

You keep adjusting yourself just to keep the relationship peaceful.

Ask yourself something uncomfortable:

Are you actually at peace, or have you simply become very good at avoiding their reactions?

A healthy relationship shouldn't require you to shrink yourself just to prevent someone else's anger.

Love Shouldn't Require You to Lose Yourself

The tricky thing about unhealthy relationships is that they don't always begin badly.

Someone can be caring before becoming controlling.

Someone can be affectionate before becoming manipulative.

Someone can make you feel deeply loved before their behaviour starts crossing boundaries.

That's why looking only at how someone makes you feel isn't enough.

Look at their patterns.

Do they respect your boundaries?

Can you disagree without being punished?

Can you have friends and family outside the relationship?

Can you say no without being manipulated?

Can you express hurt without being made to feel crazy?

Because sometimes the question isn't:

“Do they love me?”

It's:

“What does their love require me to tolerate?”

And that's a very different question.

What do you think is the most commonly ignored relationship red flag?

Drop your answer in the comments. You might mention something someone else has been struggling to recognise.

title: Your SaaS Homepage Should Not Feel Like Homework
excerpt: Most SaaS homepages look like a crowded airport terminal. 🛑 Every button is screaming for attention. There are ten animations running at the same time. And after scrolling for two minutes, nobody kno…
content:
Most SaaS homepages look like a crowded airport terminal. 🛑
Every button is screaming for attention.

There are ten animations running at the same time.

And after scrolling for two minutes, nobody knows what the software actually does.
If you run a B2B or fintech SaaS, stop making your visitors do homework.

Here is the exact 5-section homepage structure that turns confused visitors into paying users:

1. The Hero Section (5-Second Rule): One bold headline explaining the exact outcome you deliver, one plain-English subhead, and a clear button to start. No rotating banners.

2. The Social Proof Bar: Logos of tools you integrate with or companies that trust you. Put this right where their eyes land next to kill hesitation early.

3. The "Before vs. After" Pain Point: Show the ugly, manual spreadsheet mess they deal with today, then show how your tool makes it disappear.

4. The 3-Step Walkthrough: People fear long setups. Show them it only takes three simple steps to get their first win inside the app.

5. The Objections & Final Call: Answer their top three hesitations (pricing, security, contract lock-in), followed by one last, uncluttered sign-up button.

A great software homepage is not an art gallery.
It is a clean, quiet hallway that leads straight to the checkout door. 🚪

Action for today:
Open your SaaS homepage right now. Can a stranger tell what problem you solve and who it is for in under five seconds? If not, trim section one today.

Let us discuss:
What is the biggest thing that makes you leave a SaaS website instantly? Tell me below! 👇

#SaaS #WebDesign #Copywriting #B2B #KeepItSimple

title: 5 Skills Every Graduate Needs Beyond a University Degree
excerpt: 5 Skills Every Graduate Needs Beyond a University DegreeGetting a university degree is a great achievement, but the learning should not stop when you graduate.T…
content:
5 Skills Every Graduate Needs Beyond a University Degree

Getting a university degree is a great achievement, but the learning should not stop when you graduate.

The job market is changing, and employers increasingly look for people who can do more than present a certificate.

Here are five skills every graduate should start developing:

1. Communication

Knowing how to express your ideas clearly can help you in interviews, teamwork, presentations, and everyday professional life.

2. Digital Skills

You don't have to become a programmer. Learn how to use digital tools that are relevant to your career, such as Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, social media platforms, or industry-specific software.

3. Research Skills

Being able to find reliable information, compare sources, and separate facts from misinformation is valuable in almost every profession.

4. Problem-Solving

Employers want people who can look at a problem, think critically, and find practical solutions instead of simply waiting for instructions.

5. Adaptability

Technology and workplaces change quickly. Being willing to learn new skills can make it easier to adjust to new opportunities and challenges.

Your Degree Is the Beginning

Your university degree can open a door, but the skills you develop can help you stay in the room.

Start with one skill today. Learn it, practise it, and find a way to use it in a real project.

Which of these five skills do you think Nigerian graduates need the most?
