title: Wanted Ex-Gov Sylva Summoned Again Over Alleged $14.86m Fraud
excerpt: Former Bayelsa State Governor Timipre Sylva is once again in the EFCC's crosshairs after the agency renewed its call for him to turn himself in over an alleged …
content:
Former Bayelsa State Governor Timipre Sylva is once again in the EFCC's crosshairs after the agency renewed its call for him to turn himself in over an alleged $14.86 million fraud case. Sylva, who governed Bayelsa from 2007 to 2012 and later served as Minister of State for Petroleum Resources, was declared wanted by the EFCC back in November 2025 over allegations of conspiracy and dishonest conversion of funds, reportedly after he failed to honor administrative bail conditions. In May 2026, a Federal High Court in Abuja went further, granting an interim forfeiture order over nine properties linked to him.

The story took a political turn this week when Sylva announced his resignation from the All Progressives Congress (APC) on Monday, August 31. In his resignation letter addressed to his ward chairman in Bayelsa but deliberately copied to the EFCC he accused the commission of behaving "more as an organ of the APC than as an institution of State," and criticized the Tinubu administration for disappointing Nigerians.

The EFCC didn't let the accusation slide. Spokesman Dele Oyewale responded. "He has been declared wanted, he should make himself available to the commission" making clear that a resignation letter and public criticism don't change his legal status. The commission has previously denied that its investigation is politically motivated.The situation remains unresolved, with Sylva yet to appear before the commission.

title: DJ Cuppy Redefines Legacy. From Billionaire Heiress to Nigeria's Philanthropy Blueprint
excerpt: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola, known worldwide as DJ Cuppy, visits Majidun Grammar School in Lagos with bags of school supplies. The …
content:
Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola, known worldwide as DJ Cuppy, visits Majidun Grammar School in Lagos with bags of school supplies. The visit, carried out under her long running partnership with Save the Children. It was a beautiful experience seeing the Afrobeats star spend time directly in the classroom, handing out learning materials and taking on a teaching role for the day rather than simply making an appearance.

Beyond the pens and notebooks, Cuppy used the moment to talk about a much bigger personal milestone, her ambition to set foot in 50 countries. She's currently at 27 and counting, a number that reflects not just a love of travel but the reach of her charitable work, which has taken her from Nigerian classrooms to stages and summits around the globe.

The Majidun visit fits a pattern that's defined much of Cuppy's public life over the past several years using her platform and resources to push access to education, particularly for children in underserved communities. As she looked back on her philanthropic journey during the visit, it was clear the work isn't a side project for her, it's become as central to her identity as the music that made her famous in the first place.

title: Bargain of the season. Bradley Barcola joined Liverpool from PSG.
excerpt: Liverpool have pulled off one of the boldest moves of the summer window, agreeing a deal to sign Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain. The France internati…
content:
Liverpool have pulled off one of the boldest moves of the summer window, agreeing a deal to sign Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain. The France international will pen a five-year contract at Anfield, with Liverpool paying a guaranteed £106m up front and add-ons potentially pushing the total package to £123m. It's a deal that reflects months of persistence. PSG had earlier rejected multiple approaches and insisted the winger was "untransferable," but a shifting valuation gap and Barcola's own openness to a fresh challenge eventually broke the deadlock.

At just 23, Barcola arrives with serious pedigree. He was a key figure in PSG's historic winning campaign, contributing goals and assists in some of the biggest games in European football, and he's shown he can thrive under pressure on the continent's biggest stages.

Financially, this now ranks as one of Liverpool's biggest ever investments, trailing only their club record capture of Alexander Isak. But given Barcola's age, upside, and proven big match temperament, many will view this as shrewd business rather than reckless spending. The next season is going to be so thrilling, let’s see what he brings to Liverpool.

title: Modern CSS Mastery in 2026: Subgrid, Container Queries, and :has() Selector
excerpt: Explore the powerful new CSS features that make layout building and responsive component design easier and cleaner than ever before.
content:
Modern CSS Mastery in 2026: Subgrid, Container Queries, and :has() Selector

CSS has experienced a massive renaissance over recent years. Features that once required complex JavaScript observers or rigid framework hacks are now natively supported across all modern browsers.

1. CSS Container Queries (@container)

Traditional media queries evaluate the viewport width. Container queries allow components to adapt their layout based on the size of their parent container, making components truly reusable across sidebars, cards, and hero sections.

.card-container {
  container-type: inline-size;
}

@container (min-width: 400px) {
  .card-content {
    display: flex;
    flex-direction: row;
  }
}

2. The Parent Selector: :has()

The :has() pseudo-class allows styling an element based on its descendants or following siblings:

/* Style form group if it contains an invalid input */
.form-group:has(input:invalid) {
  border-color: red;
}

title: It's Okay to Cry Whenever You're Overwhelmed
excerpt: It's okay to cry whenever you're overwhelmed.You don't always need to be strong.Sometimes, you've held everything together for so long that your body simply dec…
content:
It's okay to cry whenever you're overwhelmed.

You don't always need to be strong.

Sometimes, you've held everything together for so long that your body simply decides it has had enough. The tears come, and suddenly you're wondering why you're crying over something that seems so small.

But maybe it isn't small.

Maybe it's the exam you've been stressing about, the argument you haven't gotten over, the money you're worried about, the friendship that's falling apart, the relationship that's confusing you, or the twenty other things you've been carrying quietly.

Sometimes the thing that makes you cry isn't even the real reason you're crying. It's just the final drop.

And that's okay.

We've somehow turned crying into something embarrassing. We tell ourselves to hold it in, wipe our faces quickly, and get back to whatever we were doing.

But crying doesn't mean you're weak.

It doesn't mean you're dramatic.

It doesn't mean you can't handle life.

Sometimes it simply means you're overwhelmed and you need a moment to let everything out.

You don't have to explain every tear or act tough because you are a man.

You don't have to apologize for crying.

You don't have to wait until you're completely broken before you're allowed to release something.

Find somewhere safe. Cry if you need to. Take a breath. Drink some water. Rest.

Then, when you're ready, get back up.

You can be strong and still cry.

You can be happy and still cry.

You can be capable and still have moments where everything feels like too much.

You're human. You're allowed to have a limit.

So the next time the tears come, don't be so quick to fight them.

Maybe your mind isn't failing you.

Maybe it's simply asking you to pause.

title: Am I Weird? How I Screwed My First Date (1)
excerpt: I should have kept walking.
content:
I've never been a fan of bold love. I'd rather love secretly and suppress the butterflies in my stomach while feeding myself with the lies that I'm not in love.

I was 18 and shy, drenched in thought while walking back from class when I bumped into this guy. I rushed to say sorry because it was my fault. I wasn't looking at where I was going.

I wanted the awkward moment to pass quickly. I tried to walk past him when he dragged my hand back.

“Can I speak with you?”

I was angry at myself for not looking properly. I shouldn't have been in this situation at all.

I thought, Since I'm here, let's hear him out.

“Okay, two minutes.”

“Thank you.”

He introduced himself.

I don't remember everything he said after that. Maybe because I was too busy wondering why a stranger had stopped me in the first place.

Then he asked for my number.

My brain immediately started doing overtime.

Why does he want my number?

Should I give it to him?

What if he's just being friendly?

What if he's not?

I eventually gave it to him.

And that was how I accidentally gave a stranger access to my peace of mind.

We started talking.

Nothing serious at first. Just random conversations that somehow became something I looked forward to.

I'd see his name pop up on my phone and suddenly, the butterflies I'd spent so much time denying would start doing their thing.

But I still refused to admit I liked him.

Me?

In love?

Absolutely not.

I was simply enjoying the conversation.

At least, that's what I told myself.

Until one day, he asked me out.

And this was where everything went wrong.

Because apparently, liking someone in your head is very different from actually having to sit across from them in real life.

I said yes.

I don't know why.

Maybe I was curious.

Maybe I liked him more than I wanted to admit.

Or maybe, at 18, I simply had no idea what I was getting myself into.

Either way, I agreed to the date.

And then I started panicking.

What was I supposed to wear?

What was I supposed to say?

What if there were awkward silences?

What if he looked at me and suddenly realized I was actually boring?

I spent so much time worrying about the date that I forgot the most important question:

What exactly was I going to do when I got there?

And honestly...

I should have asked myself that before saying yes.

Because I was about to screw up my first date.

To be continued.

title:
PART TWO

When Life Began to Change
excerpt: Before the pain, there was love. Before the struggle, there was home.
content:
She was the kind of person who would rather go without something herself if it meant making someone else happy. She would put her own needs aside, sometimes even denying herself the things she wanted, just to make another person smile or feel important.

But as she grew older, life began teaching her that being selfless did not mean life would always be kind to her.

Her story continued in the village.

She grew up surrounded by the simple life of the countryside, spending a lot of her time taking care of her grandmother. From a young age, she learned responsibility. She worked, helped with chores, and slowly began to understand what it meant to contribute to a family.

She also spent time living with her father.

Her education started in the village, where she attended one of the best schools around—a private school. She was determined to learn and make something of herself, even though life around her was simple.

Outside school, she helped her father at his shop.

Those were some of the moments she would later remember with mixed emotions. At that time, they were simply a family living their lives together. She helped at the shop, they ate together, went to church together, and shared whatever they had.

Her father did his best to provide for them.

But their family story was complicated.

Her father had three wives, though he did not marry all three at the same time. He first married his second wife, but that marriage eventually ended. Later, he married the woman who remained by his side and became his third wife.

She was the woman who eventually gave him the two sons he had.

For a while, they lived together as one family.

There were days when everything felt normal. They went to church together. They ate whatever was available. They laughed, lived, and shared the little things that made life feel complete.

At that point, she probably never imagined how quickly everything could change.

Because sometimes, life doesn’t warn you before it takes a turn.

Then, one day, her father became sick.

The sickness came quietly, but its arrival marked the beginning of a completely different chapter in her life.

The family that once moved through life together was about to face something none of them were prepared for.

And for her, this was only the beginning.

title: A failed failure.

It is probably another failed failure that you will try again and one day it will come out successful. I know the word is quite convincing and nobody wants to experience failure. But the beautiful thing about life is all the challenges we have faced and thought we wouldn’t pull through, we eventually did and somehow we tell our experiences to others to make them stay hopeful.

title: 8:55 AM and These Two Were in Love
excerpt: I  was late for work. They were early for romance.
content:
I had to get to the office by 9 a.m.

8:55 a.m., I was still on the road in an endless ride because the bus — korope I entered had apparently decided that today was not a day for speed.

It would stop.

Pick someone.

Move for a few seconds.

Stop again.

Drop someone.

Pick another person.

Stop again.

At this point, I wasn't sure if we were going to the office or conducting a census.

I was already angry.

I kept checking the time like somehow staring at 8:55 would make it turn back to 8:30.

Then I noticed something happening behind me.

At first, I ignored it.

I mean, everybody has their business and I had mine: getting to work before 9.

But these two people behind me clearly had a different agenda for the morning.

They were in love.

Inside the korope.

In broad daylight.

With the rest of us as their unwilling audience.

I tried to mind my business.

You know that thing where you suddenly become very interested in looking through the window because you don't want to see what is happening beside you?

That was me.

But these people were not helping.

The bus was already moving like we had all signed an agreement to arrive at our destinations whenever God deemed fit, and these two had decided to add romance to the journey.

I was late.

The driver was slow.

And somehow, these two people had found the perfect time to be in love.

I wanted to turn around and tell them,

“Please, some of us are trying to get to work.”

But then I started wondering...

Why was I even angry?

Maybe they weren't doing anything wrong.

Maybe they were just two people enjoying each other's company.

Maybe the bus was their little date spot.

Maybe,

No.

I was still late. 😭

And that's how a normal morning commute turned into one of those stories you don't plan to tell anyone but somehow end up telling everybody.

Sometimes, it's not even the big things that make a day memorable.

Sometimes, it's a stubborn korope, a 9 a.m. deadline, and two lovers who clearly forgot they were in public.

Anyway, if you're reading this and you were one of those lovers...

I hope you got home safely.

But please.

Next time, remember the rest of us are also going somewhere. 😂

title: Copy of The Night We Played Truth or Dare
excerpt: It was supposed to be just a game
content:
It was a few minutes past 10 p.m. My eyes were still wide open despite having a stressful day in school. I'd finished all my chores so I could use my mum's phone without interruption.

I got chatting with my stranger friend, and everything was going smoothly until he asked if we could play Truth or Dare. I agreed because I'd always heard my friends talk about their funny dare experiences.

After all, I wanted the experience too.

We started with truth. The questions were harmless.

"What's your favourite colour?"

"Who's your celebrity crush?"

"Have you ever had a boyfriend?"

We laughed through every answer, and somehow it made us even more comfortable with each other.

Then we switched to dares.

"Change your profile picture for five minutes."

"Send a random emoji."

Easy enough.

But as the game went on, the dares became more personal.

He asked me to send a picture. At first, it sounded innocent, so I did. Then another. Then another.

Before I knew it, the requests became uncomfortable.

He kept saying things like, "Come on, it's just a game," or, "Don't you trust me?"

I remember staring at my screen, wondering why I suddenly felt uneasy. I didn't want to seem rude or boring, but deep down, I knew I didn't want to do what he was asking.

So...

I refused.

The atmosphere changed almost immediately.

The friendly guy I'd spent weeks talking to suddenly felt like someone else. His replies became cold. The jokes disappeared. The warmth I'd grown used to was gone.

I kept wondering what I'd done wrong.

Was I overreacting?

Had I ruined the friendship over a simple game?

For the next few days, our conversations were never the same. The excitement faded, and so did the person I thought I knew.

I couldn't explain it, but I had a feeling that the game we'd just played had changed something between us.

I was right.

I just didn't know how much it would change.

To be continued...

title: The Stranger Who Became My Friend
excerpt: The conversations that made a stranger feel like home.
content:
I said that was only the beginning because who would have thought that a random stranger I met on Facebook one cold Tuesday evening would become my friend?

We started chatting, and for a girl who didn't know much, at least not yet, he filled a void I didn't even know existed.

You could tell how excited I was every time we texted. It didn't feel like I was talking to a stranger anymore. We just clicked.

The conversations flowed effortlessly. The energy was there, the vibe was unmatched, and talking to him felt like I'd known him my whole life.

I didn't mind if my Mum's old android phone, which lagged almost all the time, wasn't available. I'd gladly pick up my Dad's button phone and spend what felt like forever trying to connect to Facebook. On a bad day, it could take ages. On a good day, it loaded just fast enough to keep me smiling.

I didn't even mind the stress of typing by pressing the same button over and over just to get the right letter.

And I definitely didn't enjoy the heartbreaking moments when I accidentally pressed the cancel button and watched my carefully typed message disappear.

None of it mattered.

Not the slow internet.

Not the lagging phones.

Not the frustration of starting a message all over again.

As long as I could talk to my stranger.

Back then, all I saw was a friend.

I had no idea that this friendship would eventually teach me one of the biggest lessons of my life.

To be continued...

title: The strangest thing about learning technology is that every answer seems to come with three more questions.
excerpt: I used to think there would be a point where everything would finally start making sense.A point where cybersecurity wouldn't feel so unfamiliar.Where artificia…
content:
I used to think there would be a point where everything would finally start making sense.

A point where cybersecurity wouldn't feel so unfamiliar.

Where artificial intelligence wouldn't leave me with ten more things to research after learning one thing.

Where the digital world would stop feeling like a place I was constantly trying to catch up with.

I haven't reached that point.

And I'm beginning to wonder if anyone ever really does.

I've spent the past few years finding my way through unfamiliar spaces cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, web development, and everything that seems to live between them.

I've met people who introduced me to ideas I didn't even know existed.

I've discovered solutions to problems I didn't know I had.

I've learned something, felt that little satisfaction of "Okay, I finally get it," only to stumble into something else that reminded me just how much I still didn't know.

Sometimes, it has been exciting.

Sometimes, completely overwhelming.

And sometimes, I've wondered if everyone else somehow received a manual that I missed.

But the more I learn, the more I realize something:

Maybe there is no manual.

Technology keeps changing. New problems keep appearing. Things we once understood get challenged. Things we thought were impossible become ordinary.

So perhaps the goal was never to figure it all out.

Perhaps it's to keep asking questions.

To keep learning.

To keep unlearning.

To stay curious enough to walk into unfamiliar territory without feeling like you have to already know the way.

That's where I am right now.

Still learning.

Still questioning.

Still finding my way.

And somewhere along the way, I realized that maybe the things I'm learning, questioning, and discovering are worth documenting—not because I have all the answers, but because someone else might be asking the same questions.

Maybe we're all just a little further along in different parts of the journey.

And maybe that's enough to keep going.

title: I Asked AI to Think for Me. It Couldn't. That's When I Understood Its Real Power.
excerpt: A few months ago, I thought AI was either going to replace everyone or magically solve all my problems.The internet wasn't helping.One person called it the futu…
content:
A few months ago, I thought AI was either going to replace everyone or magically solve all my problems.

The internet wasn't helping.

One person called it the future.

Another called it the end of creativity.

Some people swore it would take our jobs. Others treated it like a genius that never gets anything wrong.

So I decided to stop listening to everyone else.

I opened an AI chatbot and started asking questions.

At first, it felt impressive.

It answered in seconds.

It explained difficult ideas.

It even helped me organize my thoughts.

Then I made a mistake.

I stopped thinking.

Instead of using AI to improve my ideas, I started expecting it to have the ideas for me.

That's when everything it gave me started feeling... empty.

The words were there.

The structure was there.

But something was missing.

Me.

That's when I realized something we don't talk about enough.

AI doesn't replace curiosity.

It rewards it.

If you ask lazy questions, you'll probably get average answers.

If you ask thoughtful questions, challenge the responses, and add your own perspective, AI becomes something completely different.

Not your replacement.

Your assistant.

Technology has always worked this way.

A calculator never replaced mathematicians.

A camera never replaced photographers.

Google never replaced teachers.

The people who benefited the most weren't the ones who feared the technology.

They were the ones who learned how to use it well.

I think AI is following the same path.

The question isn't whether AI will change the way we work.

It already has.

The real question is whether we'll let it make us passive or push us to become even more creative.

Because the best ideas still begin with people.

AI can help shape them.

But it can't replace the experiences, emotions, and perspectives that make those ideas worth sharing.

Maybe that's the real future of AI.

Not humans versus machines.

Humans working smarter with them.

How has AI changed the way you learn or work? We'd love to hear your experience in the comments

title: This Might Be for Someone Else, Not Just Me.
excerpt: You don't have to have the right words. You just have to have something to say.Maybe you're scared. Maybe you're showing up all professional and polished. Maybe…
content:
You don't have to have the right words. You just have to have something to say.

Maybe you're scared. Maybe you're showing up all professional and polished. Maybe you just came for the vibe, no pressure, no plan. Whatever brought you here welcome. Echogist is the place for you.

Life doesn't wait for you to feel ready before it hands you something to process. So whether you're ranting about your day, venting about that Lagos traffic that stole two hours of your life, nursing a heartbreak, or just sitting with a feeling you can't quite name yet we're here. Not as strangers scrolling past, but as a community that shows up with you through it all. The happy days. The sad days. The days you're winning and don't even know how you did it. The days you're barely holding it together.

Think of this as your journal except this one talks back. This one holds you.

And here's the thing about writing that most people don't realize until they've lived it, it's never just words on a page. What you write today, in your rawest, most honest moment, could be the exact sentence someone else needed to read tomorrow. Your heartbreak could be someone else's healing. Your rant could be someone else's relief. Your quiet 2am thought could be the reason someone doesn't feel so alone tonight.

So no this was never just about you. It's about every person who stumbles onto your story. Every person who sees your notification pop up and feels a small glimmer of “okay maybe I'm not the only one”.

That's the kind of community we're building. Not a platform. A place.

So once again, welcome to Echogist. A place for all of us, the scared, the polished, the heartbroken, the healed, the still figuring it out.

We can't wait to see what you bring here. We are so, so excited to have you.

title: The Rise of the Agent Architect
excerpt: monolithic agent and a multi-agent orchestration
content:
As we hit the midpoint of 2026, the landscape of AI automation has undergone a fundamental shift. We are no longer just prompting models to give us answers; we are architecting systems where multiple AI agents collaborate to solve complex business problems.

The choice between a monolithic agent and a multi-agent orchestration layer like LangGraph or n8n is now the most critical decision an automation engineer makes. Monolithic agents are fast to deploy but often struggle with long-term reliability and complex state management. On the other hand, multi-agent swarms allow for granular control, easier debugging, and the ability to integrate human-in-the-loop checkpoints effectively.

This transition marks the professionalization of our field. We are moving from being AI enthusiasts to becoming AI systems architects. The focus has shifted from the quality of the individual LLM output to the robustness of the orchestration logic connecting them.

What does your current stack look like? Are you sticking with visual builders like n8n, or have you moved into code-first orchestration with frameworks like LangGraph?

title:
PART ONE

Before Life Changed Everything
excerpt: A little girl, a struggling family, and the beginning of a story no one could have predicted.
content:
Before she became the woman she would one day be, she was simply a little girl born in a small village.

She was born a twin.

But she would not grow up with her twin.

Her twin died, leaving her to continue the journey alone.

She was only five years old when another painful change came into her life—her mother left.

At that age, she was too young to understand everything that was happening around her. Her family was struggling financially, and life was difficult.

Her father was left to do everything he could to provide for his children.

He worked hard, riding bicycles and motorcycles for other people and taking whatever work he could find. He didn’t have much, but he kept pushing.

And slowly, his efforts began to pay off.

Years later, the man who had once struggled to survive became a landlord with six shops. The family had their own house, and he even provided a borehole for them.

It was not wealth handed to him.

It was something he built through years of hard work.

After her mother left, her father’s sister took her in. She helped raise her, cared for her, and made sure she went to school.

Eventually, after completing primary school, the little girl returned to the village to stay with her grandmother.

And although she had already experienced loss at such a young age, there was something remarkable about her.

She was strong.

She was fearless.

She didn’t easily allow anyone to intimidate her. In school and around the village, she was known as the kind of girl who would stand her ground.

She could fight.

She could defend herself.

And she certainly wasn’t afraid of anybody’s face.

But behind that fearless little girl was a child who had already experienced things she was too young to fully understand—a lost twin, an absent mother, a struggling father, and a childhood spent moving between the people who cared for her.

She didn’t know it then, but every one of those experiences was quietly shaping her.

Her story had only just begun. ❤️

title: Normalize helping people first instead of taking a video of them
excerpt: Honestly, in Nigeria, we don't take helping people seriously enough. Sometimes, someone is crying, injured, stranded, or clearly in need of help, and instead of rushing to help, the first thing we do…
content:
Honestly, in Nigeria, we don't take helping people seriously enough.

Sometimes, someone is crying, injured, stranded, or clearly in need of help, and instead of rushing to help, the first thing we do is bring out our phones.

Camera on.

Recording.

“Guys, look at what is happening…” and somehow, the person who needs help becomes content.

Don't get me wrong, social media attention can be useful. Sharing someone's situation online can help them get assistance, raise awareness, or even connect them with people who can actually help. There is nothing wrong with documenting something when it serves a purpose but there is a problem when recording becomes more important than helping.

If someone is lying helplessly on the road, what they need first is not a camera in their face. They need someone to check if they're okay, call for help, move them away from danger if it is safe to do so, or simply stay with them until help arrives.

If someone is being harassed or attacked, don't stand there recording the whole thing while shouting, “This is happening in Nigeria!”

Abeggg, help the person first.

We have become so used to documenting everything that sometimes we forget there is an actual human being behind the video.

Not every painful moment needs to become content. Not every emergency needs an audience before it gets a response.

Sometimes, the best thing you can do is put your phone down and use your hands.

Help first and Record later because at the end of the day, a viral video cannot replace a life that could have been saved.

title: Normalize Not Waiting Until Birthdays to Tell People You Love Them
excerpt: Normalize not waiting until birthdays to tell people how much they mean to you and that you love them.Why do we need a special occasion to tell someone they mat…
content:
Normalize not waiting until birthdays to tell people how much they mean to you and that you love them.

Why do we need a special occasion to tell someone they matter to us?

We wait for birthdays, anniversaries, Valentine's Day, Mother's Day, Father's Day, and every other day society has given us permission to be sentimental.

But what about an ordinary Tuesday or Friday?

What about texting your friend in the middle of the afternoon just to say, "I really appreciate having you in my life"?

What about calling your mother and telling her you love her without needing anything from her?

What about looking at your best friend and saying, "You know I really love you, right?"

Or reminding your father that you really appreciate his presence in your life.

It shouldn't feel strange.

We often assume people already know how we feel about them. And maybe they do. But sometimes, hearing the words still means something.

There is a difference between knowing someone loves you and hearing them say it.

Life is unpredictable. We don't know how many more conversations we'll have with the people we love. We don't know when an ordinary day will become a memory.

So why are we saving all our affection for special occasions?

You don't need a birthday cake in front of someone before you're allowed to tell them how much they mean to you.

You don't need a holiday.

You don't need a long paragraph.

Sometimes, a simple "I'm glad you're in my life" is enough.

Tell your parents you love them.

Thank the friend who has always shown up.

Appreciate the person who makes your difficult days a little easier.

And don't wait until you have the perfect words.

Say it while they're here to hear it.

title: You, Me and the Elevator
excerpt: Part Two
content:
“Please, sit,” I replied.

He pulled out the chair and sat across from me and he checked me out.

I no dey whine una.

He looked at me for a few seconds before smiling.

“You look stunning.”

I smiled.

Okayyyyy.

He went on to explain that he was trying to get more people to know about his business and asked if I would be interested in helping him promote it.

Apparently, that was the reason he approached me.

I won't lie, I was a little disappointed.

So this fine man didn't walk over here because he thought I was fine?

He wanted customers?

Ah. It's fine sha.

But at least he still admired me. Where I wan see another man wey go look at me like this?

We talked for a while, although I have to confess that I barely remembered half of what he said because I was too busy staring into his beautiful eyes and admiring that smile.

At the end of our little conversation, he offered to pay for my meal.

I politely declined. C'mon girl!

I'm an independent woman, thank you very much.

He only grinned, pulled a business card from his pocket and placed it on the table.

“Have a nice evening.”

Then he left.

I sighed disappointedly.

I stared at the card for a moment before leaving it exactly where he had placed it.

I wasn't going to call him.

Obviously.

I went home that evening tired, but strangely happy.

At least I finally ticked off this month's solo date.

The next morning, I rushed into work running on barely enough sleep. I tried to finish the last episode of "Vagabond" a K-drama series.

I was already late to work .

I hurried toward the elevator just as the doors were closing.

I squeezed myself in and then,

BAM.

Something hard collided with me.

My bag fell to the floor, and everything inside scattered.

“Seriously?” I muttered furiously as I bent down to pick up my things.

Another person bent down to help me.

“I'm sorry. I wasn't looking where I was going.”

I froze. That voice.

I slowly raised my head.

The restaurant guy was the one in front of me.

He's helping me pick my stuff littered on the floor.

He smiled.

“You,” I whispered.

He smiled wider, “Apparently, we keep running into each other.”

title: The Skill You Keep Ignoring Might Be Your Opportunity
excerpt: Discover it. Develop it. Use it.
content:
Sometimes, we think opportunities will come from somewhere outside us.

We wait for a job.

We wait for someone to recommend us.

We wait for a big company to notice us.

We wait until we have the “right” qualifications before we start.

But sometimes, the opportunity is already hiding inside a skill we have been taking for granted.

Maybe you are good at writing.

Maybe you know how to design simple graphics.

Maybe you are good at selling.

Maybe you can explain difficult things in a simple way.

Maybe you are good at talking to people, organising things, researching, creating videos or using social media.

These skills may seem ordinary to you because you use them every day.

But something being easy for you does not mean it has no value.

Start paying attention to what you can do.

One of the biggest mistakes you can make is waiting until someone tells you that your skill is valuable.

Start practising it.

Improve it.

Use it to solve a problem.

Create something with it.

Share your work.

And most importantly, stop hiding while you are still learning.

You don't have to become an expert before you start.

Your first article may not be perfect.

Your first design may not look professional.

Your first business attempt may not make much money.

Your first video may barely get views.

That's okay.

You are building evidence of what you can do.

And sometimes, that evidence becomes the thing that attracts your next opportunity.

Your skill may not look like an opportunity yet.

It may simply look like something you enjoy doing.

But with practice, consistency and the right direction, that skill can become a service, a business, a career or even an opportunity you never expected.

So ask yourself today:

What am I good at that I haven't taken seriously enough?

Maybe it's time to stop overlooking it.

Start small. Build the skill. Show your work. See where it takes you.

title: HOW A GOAL CELEBRATION NEARLY DEPRIVED A TEAM OF QUALIFICATION
excerpt: A player scored a goal that sent his country to a semi-final, took his shirt off to celebrate, and in that one moment turned his team's qualification into a lottery. That is exactly what happened to O…
content:
A player scored a goal that sent his country to a semi-final, took his shirt off to celebrate, and in that one moment turned his team's qualification into a lottery. That is exactly what happened to Oman at the Gulf Cup on Tuesday.

In their last Group A match, Oman needed to beat Kuwait and hope Iraq lost to Saudi Arabia. Both of those things happened. Oman won 3-1, Iraq lost 2-0, and the two teams finished level on four points. Their head-to-head game had ended 1-1, and both had scored four goals and conceded five across the group.

So it came down to fair play. Before Oman's third goal, they had seven yellow cards to Iraq's eight, which meant Oman were going through. Then Musab Al-Shaqsi scored that third goal in the 84th minute and pulled off his shirt to celebrate.

Now, under Law 12 of the Laws of the Game, a player who removes his shirt while celebrating a goal must be cautioned. The goal still stands, but the yellow card is automatic. The referee had no choice. That one card took Oman to eight, level with Iraq, with no red cards on either side.

At that point, nothing was left to separate them. The Gulf Cup's own tournament regulations, set by the Arabian Gulf Cup Football Federation, list the tiebreakers in this order: head-to-head results, then goal difference and goals scored across all group matches, then disciplinary points, and finally a drawing of lots. So the organisers held a draw at a hotel in Jeddah, and Oman came out on top.

This is where FIFA comes in. For the 2026 World Cup, FIFA changed its tiebreakers. Under Article 13 of the World Cup regulations, teams still level after head-to-head results, overall goals and the team conduct score are ranked using the most recent FIFA World Ranking. The drawing of lots, the final fallback at every previous World Cup, was replaced. FIFA had already started moving in that direction at the 2025 Arab Cup.

If the Gulf Cup had followed FIFA's approach, Iraq would be in the semi-final right now. They are ranked 63rd in the world, while Oman are 80th. But the Gulf Cup federation chose to keep the drawing of lots, and as the organiser of its own competition, it is entitled to do that. FIFA's World Cup regulations govern the World Cup. They do not automatically bind a regional tournament like the Gulf Cup.

And this is not the first time fair play has decided something big. At the 2018 World Cup, Senegal went out because they had two more yellow cards than Japan, and they became the first team ever eliminated from a World Cup on fair play.

So which system is fairer? A draw gives both teams an equal chance, but it leaves a football result to pure luck. A ranking rewards a team's record over years, but it can feel like punishing the smaller nation for results that came long before the tournament. I lean towards the ranking, because at least it is based on something a team actually did on the pitch. But I understand why the Gulf Cup federation sees it differently.

One thing is not up for debate. Al-Shaqsi scored a beautiful goal, and then his shirt nearly cost his country everything. Players, please keep your shirts on.

title: The Ultimate Guide to Securing High-Paying Global Remote Tech Jobs
excerpt: Actionable strategies for engineers and designers worldwide to stand out, pass asynchronous evaluations, and land international remote roles paying USD.
content:
The Ultimate Guide to Securing High-Paying Global Remote Tech Jobs

The global tech hiring landscape has permanently transitioned to distributed teams. Companies in North America and Europe actively recruit top engineering and design talent worldwide. However, succeeding in the international remote market requires a distinct strategy.

1. Developing Asynchronous Communication Prowess

Remote teams thrive on asynchronous documentation. Clear, concise, and structured written communication is often valued as much as raw coding capability. Demonstrate your communication skills through well-crafted GitHub PR descriptions, engineering blog posts, and detailed project documentation.

2. Building a Proof-of-Work Portfolio

A generic resume listing buzzwords rarely stands out. Create 2–3 deployed, full-stack open-source projects that solve real problems. Include Loom walkthrough videos demonstrating your architecture and live demo links.

3. Where to Find Legitimate Remote Opportunities

  • Wellfound (formerly AngelList Talent): Premier platform for early-stage and hyper-growth venture-backed startups.
  • RemoteOK & We Work Remotely: Curated remote-first job boards.
  • Direct Networking on LinkedIn & X: Follow founders and engineering managers who tweet about open hiring needs before job listings go public.

title: The most difficult decision I ever made.
excerpt: This might be the most difficult decision I ever made. I just hope I don’t regret it.
content:
Late 2021 to mid 2022, eight whole month, non stop, that's how long it took me to wrote my first book. A 25k words novella. It was my masterpiece at the time. There are no much publishing house for unsolicited novella submissions, so my options were limited. But I didn't let that discourage me, I finished the book, redrafted a couple of times till I felt it was ready.

I had my final draft, bio, and synopsis. Then I got to submitting. After two days, I've exhausted my options and now it's a waiting game. Most publishers didn't reply (well, that was expected), a couple did but with rejection letters (didn’t phase me), but one stood out, it was a review, a good review. Paraphrasing, “we love your book, the idea and writing style unfortunately there are too much work to be done on it. Redraft and resubmit, then we might consider you”

I nearly went mental with excitement, because to me that was a win, a very big win. I didn’t think I was good enough but that review gave me courage and hope. Well, I had a couple of months before their submission window closes so I get to redrafting. I did my best and resubmitted a couple of weeks later. Unfortunately, I still wasn’t good enough so I got a final rejection letter.

Then, I had to divert my attention to something else; hustle and school so I didn't write for a couple years. I didn’t exactly quit but I put my writing journey on hold.

This year I decided to go back to writing fully (currently on my second and third book). I took the time to redraft the novella and submitted it to another publishing house. Luckily, it was accepted and i was offered a publishing deal, BUT I had to turn it down.

Why? You might ask. This is what I've been chasing for so long. Well, this new publishing house is going use AI to alter my book. I don't care to what extent, I can't have that. So I turn down the deal and now, I'm back to querying.

I just hope I made the right decision.

title: Veteran Nollywood Actor Olu Jacobs Dies at 84
excerpt: Veteran Nigerian actor and film executive Oludotun Baiyewun Jacobs, popularly known as Olu Jacobs, has died at the age of 84. His death was announced on Wedne…
content:
Veteran Nigerian actor and film executive Oludotun Baiyewun Jacobs, popularly known as Olu Jacobs, has died at the age of 84. His death was announced on Wednesday, September 16, 2026, in a statement shared on Instagram, describing him as "The Lion of Lufodo" and saying his life was "well lived and fought." Jacobs, born July 11, 1942, was one of Nigeria's most respected actors, with a career spanning stage, television and film that began with British television productions before he became a towering figure in Nollywood.

Jacobs is survived by his wife, fellow veteran actress Joke Silva, with whom he co-founded the Lufodo Group and the Lufodo Academy of Performing Arts, an institution dedicated to training young talent in theatre and film. In recent years, Jacobs had largely stayed out of the public eye as he battled dementia, a condition Silva had spoken about publicly while continuing to protect his privacy. The family has appealed to bloggers and social media influencers to respect their privacy as they mourn, even as tributes pour in from fans and colleagues honoring one of the most influential figures in African cinema.

title: Why Most Nigerians Fail at Making Money Online — And It’s Not Because They’re Lazy
excerpt: The biggest mistakes beginners make when trying to earn online — and what to do differently.
content:
Every day, thousands of Nigerians search for ways to make money online.

They download apps.
They create accounts.
They watch YouTube videos.
They join WhatsApp groups.
They try freelancing platforms.

And after a few weeks, many of them give up.

Then someone says, “Making money online doesn’t work.”

But sometimes, the problem isn’t laziness.

The problem is the strategy.

Here are some of the biggest mistakes beginners make.

1. Chasing every opportunity they see

One day it’s surveys.

The next day it’s freelancing.

Then crypto.

Then affiliate marketing.

Then an AI side hustle.

Then another app promising easy money.

Trying different things isn’t necessarily bad, but constantly jumping from one opportunity to another makes it difficult to build meaningful experience.

Instead, choose one realistic path and give yourself enough time to understand how it works.

2. Looking for money before developing a skill

A lot of beginners ask:

“Which website pays Nigerians the most?”

That’s a useful question, but there’s another question you should ask first:

“What can I actually offer?”

Writing, graphic design, video editing, translation, social-media management, virtual assistance and other digital skills can become income sources.

A platform doesn’t create your value.

Your ability to solve a problem does.

3. Believing everything they see online

Someone posts:

“I made ₦500,000 in one week from this app!”

Immediately, hundreds of people want the same result.

But screenshots don’t tell the whole story.

Before spending money or giving personal information to an online opportunity, research it.

Look for independent reviews, understand the payment process, check the requirements, and be suspicious of platforms that demand money simply because you want to access supposed earnings.

Never let excitement replace verification.

4. Expecting instant results

This is probably one of the biggest problems.

You create a freelance profile today and expect a client tomorrow.

You publish your first article and expect thousands of readers.

You start posting videos and expect them to go viral immediately.

Sometimes it happens.

Usually, it takes time.

Building an online income can involve learning, experimenting, getting rejected, improving your work, and trying again.

Your first month might teach you more than it pays you.

That doesn’t automatically mean you’re failing.

5. Using AI without learning anything

AI has made many online tasks faster.

But there’s a difference between using AI as a tool and letting AI do all your thinking.

If you’re a writer, learn writing.

If you’re a designer, learn design.

If you’re creating videos, learn storytelling.

Then use AI to speed up your workflow.

The people who understand the skill behind the tool can often do much more with it than people who simply copy and paste AI-generated answers.

6. Never learning how to find customers

You can have a great skill and still make ₦0 if nobody knows you exist.

That’s why learning basic marketing matters.

Create samples of your work.

Post them online.

Tell people what you offer.

Contact potential clients professionally.

Ask existing clients for testimonials.

Build relationships.

Don’t just sit on a freelancing platform waiting for someone to discover you.

7. Giving up after a few failures

You apply for five jobs and get rejected.

You try three platforms and make almost nothing.

You send messages to potential clients and nobody responds.

It’s frustrating.

But rejection doesn’t necessarily mean you have nothing valuable to offer.

Sometimes your portfolio needs improvement.

Sometimes your offer isn’t clear.

Sometimes you’re targeting the wrong people.

Sometimes you simply need more attempts.

Instead of asking, “Why isn’t this working?”, ask:

“What can I change?”

That question gives you something you can actually act on.

So, what should you do instead?

Start small.

Pick one skill.

Learn it.

Practise it.

Create samples.

Find people who need it.

Offer your service.

Get feedback.

Improve.

Repeat.

You don’t need to try every opportunity on the internet.

You don’t need to become an expert overnight.

And you definitely don’t need to believe every person promising you overnight wealth.

Making money online is possible, but it isn’t magic.

Behind most sustainable online income is a simple process:

Learn → Create → Offer → Improve → Repeat.

Your first goal shouldn’t be becoming rich.

It should be becoming useful enough that someone is willing to pay you.

Once you can do that consistently, you have something much more valuable than another “money-making app.”

You have a skill.

title: What I’d Do If I Had Only a Phone and ₦0 to Start Making Money Online
excerpt: You don’t need a laptop, office, or huge capital to start. Here’s where I’d begin with just a smartphone and internet access.
content:
If I had only a smartphone, internet access, and ₦0 in my account, I wouldn’t start by searching for a magical app that pays me for doing nothing.

I’d start by asking a different question:

“What can I do with this phone that someone else would actually pay for?”

That shift in mindset can change everything.

You don’t need to become a millionaire overnight. You need to find one simple service, learn how to deliver it, and find people who need it.

Here are five things I would try.

1. Writing captions and social-media posts

Many small businesses know they need to post online but don’t know what to write.

You can offer to create captions for businesses, creators, restaurants, fashion vendors, real-estate agents, or online stores.

You can even use AI to help generate ideas, then edit the content so it sounds natural and fits the client’s brand.

Start with a few sample posts and show potential clients what you can do.

2. Canva designs

You don’t need to be a professional graphic designer to start learning Canva.

You can create simple:

  • Instagram posts

  • Flyers

  • Event graphics

  • Business announcements

  • Price lists

  • WhatsApp promotional designs

Start by practising with imaginary businesses or redesigning existing concepts for your portfolio.

The goal isn’t to pretend you’re an expert.

The goal is to become good enough to solve a simple problem for someone.

3. CV and document writing

People regularly need help presenting themselves professionally.

If you’re good at writing, you can help create or improve CVs, cover letters, biographies, LinkedIn summaries, and other professional documents.

AI can help with brainstorming and structure, but don’t simply copy and paste whatever it produces.

Edit everything, check the information, and make sure the final document actually sounds like the person you’re writing for.

4. Short-form video scripts

TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts have created a huge demand for short content.

But many creators struggle with one thing:

What should I say in the first 10 seconds?

You can offer to write short scripts with a hook, useful information, and a clear ending.

For example:

Hook: “You’re probably using ChatGPT the wrong way.”

Then explain the problem, give three useful tips, and finish with a call to action.

You don’t need to appear on camera. Your job can simply be creating the script.

5. Find businesses that need help

This is the part many beginners skip.

Creating a service is only half the job.

You also need customers.

Search Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn and WhatsApp for small businesses that have weak social-media content, inconsistent posts, poor captions, or outdated promotional materials.

Then send a short, respectful message.

Don’t spam hundreds of people with the same paragraph.

Instead, look at their business and mention something specific you noticed.

You could offer to create one sample caption or design so they can see what you can do.

The important part: don’t wait until you’re perfect

If you have ₦0, your biggest advantage is that you can start learning without spending money.

Use free resources.

Practise every day.

Build three to five samples.

Put those samples somewhere potential clients can see them.

Then start reaching out.

Your first client might not pay a huge amount.

That’s okay.

The first goal is not to become rich overnight.

The first goal is to prove that someone is willing to pay you for a useful skill.

Once you have that proof, you can improve your service, increase your prices, collect testimonials, and look for better-paying clients.

Your phone isn’t automatically a money-making machine.

But it can become a tool for learning, creating, marketing, communicating with clients, and delivering services.

And sometimes, that’s where the first ₦1,000 begins.

title: VDM vs Apostle Arome:
excerpt:
Beyond technology:
What if Nigeria's Greatest need is revival!?
content:
Nigeria is having another big conversation online and this time is about prayer, purpose and progress.

A viral sermon by Apostle Arome osayi has sparked a heated debate after he spoke about Nigeria's national calling being connected to revival and prayer, rather than simply trying to compete with other countries in technology and manufacturing.

Very Dark man (VDM) wasn't having it. He criticized the message arguing that Nigerians also need to focus on creativity, technology, innovation and practical solutions, rather than depending mainly on prayer for the country's problem. And just like that social media had another debate.

Some people agreed with VDM. others believe prayer is an important part of Nigeria's purpose and that the message was misunderstood. The recent conversation has raised an important question: what does Nigeria really need? Technology? innovation? development? Absolutely! But does that mean we should forget about prayer? NO. Nigeria needs technology, Nigerian needs creativity, needs good leadership, education, industries and people who are willing to build. But Christians also believe that God has a purpose for every nation. And perhaps this was the point Apostle Arome was trying to make when he spoke about Nigerians calling being connected to revival. A nation can have the best technology in the world and still have people who are spiritually empty. We can build skyscrapers, develop artificial intelligence, manufacture cars and create amazing inventions -but what happened to all of it when our time on earth is over?.

One day every human being will leave everything behind, the money, houses, cars, technology, fames, followers everything. And we will stand before God. The Bible reminds us in Matthew 16:26 "what profit is there if you gain the whole world- and lose internal life? what can be compared with the value of internal life? That was put everything into perspective. So perhaps the question isn't prayer or technology. maybe Nigeria needs both.

We should build, we should innovate, we should work hard but most importantly we should also pray. Because no amount of human achievements can replace God. This disagreement has also brought attention to something: how we disagree with one another. Yeah criticism is allowed, questions are allowed, even strong agreement is allowed. but as Christians, we are also called to watch our words. Jesus thought us to love one another, and that the Bible warns us about the power of the tongue. At the end of the day this conversation is bigger than all the disagreements on social media. it's about what we value. It's about what kind of nation we want to build. It's more importantly about remembering that this earth is not our final destination.

We are here for a purpose. We should build,we should work,we should learn,we should innovate but above everything else we should seek God. Because one day, when everything we've built is left behind,our relationship with God is what will matter.....!
